change.describe: branch `pr-77754` of sentry-77754 against bb5a6837cb5b3d8d3b174e17d42ec14486ef8738 (merge-base bb5a683)
change.title: pr-77754
change.description:
fix(ecosystem): Breaks issue sync cycles
Passes JSON instead of classes when queueing task
removes SourceType enum
Converts from JSON to dictionaries instead
Removes minor change made to sync utils, adds test for assignment loop
Fix typing for optional assignment_source
More typing fixes
Fixes tests, adds new test for sync loop checks
change.author: Gabe Villalobos

findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain class default, so Python evaluates `timezone.now()` once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` then carries the process start time, not the time it was queued, and `from_integration` never sets it. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The test at tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:36 only asserts `queued is not None`, so it cannot catch this.
findings.originReason: The whole file is new in this diff.

verification.reason: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain dataclass default, so it is evaluated once when the module is imported, and `from_integration` never overrides it. Nothing in src reads `queued`, so for now the wrong value has no effect on behaviour, which is why the severity is lowered.

findings.title: `from_dict` turns a malformed dict into `None` without a log, which silently disables the sync-cycle guard
findings.body: `from_dict` returns None on any TypeError. The task at src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56 treats None as 'no source', so `should_sync` skips the same-integration check (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390-391) and the assignment is echoed back to the integration that sent it. Nothing is logged, so this failure is invisible. The `ValueError` branch is also unreachable, because a dataclass constructor does not raise ValueError for wrong field values. The realistic trigger is a key mismatch between the enqueuing and consuming code. Consider logging when a non-empty dict fails to parse.
findings.originReason: The file and the task parsing are new in this change.

verification.reason: `from_dict` catches TypeError/ValueError and returns None without logging. The task then passes None into `should_sync`, which skips the same-integration check, so a dict that fails to parse would quietly re-enable the echo back to the source integration.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature but nothing passes or reads it
findings.body: The abstract `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter. The only caller, src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:44-46, does not pass it. The implementations (src/sentry/integrations/jira/integration.py:990, src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py:161) do not take it either. The parameter suggests that status sync is source-aware when it is not. Remove it, or wire it through and use it.

verification.reason: The only caller, the sync_status_outbound task, calls `installation.sync_status_outbound(external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` without passing a source. None of the concrete implementations (jira, jira_server, vsts, example) declare the new parameter, so it is unused.

findings.title: The loop test does not go through the inbound path that creates the source
findings.body: The PR says it adds a test for the assignment loop. The matching-source test builds `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` by hand and calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly (lines 215-219). The code that creates the source in production is `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96-99 and 112-116), and no test covers it with a matching integration. The deassign loop break (src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:238-240 with a source) has no test either. The comment at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:387-389 says other integrations should still sync outward, and no test asserts that.

verification.reason: Only one test uses a matching AssignmentSource, and it calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly. The inbound tests call `sync_group_assignee_inbound` but never mock or assert the outbound sync. No test covers a deassign with a source, or a source from a different integration still syncing outward.

findings.title: Is it intended that the same-integration skip also blocks other external issues from that integration?
findings.body: The check at lines 390-391 compares the integration only, not the external issue. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:135-145) loops over every linked external issue for the group. Before this PR, an assignment from one Jira issue reached the group's other Jira links. Now every link from the same integration is skipped. If a group can link two issues from one integration, the second one will silently never get the assignee. Was this intended? I did not confirm whether multiple links from one integration to one group are possible.
findings.originReason: The diff adds the integration-level skip.

verification.reason: The skip compares only integration_id, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` queues a task for every linked external issue. GroupLink is unique on (group, linked_type, linked_id) and ExternalIssue is unique on (org, integration_id, key), so one group can link several issues from the same integration. Those other links will no longer get the assignee. This looks like a design trade-off rather than a definite bug, so the severity is lowered.

contracts.action: Inbound webhook assigns a Sentry issue (sync_group_assignee_inbound with assign=True passes AssignmentSource to GroupAssignee.objects.assign)
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:112 before the PR: GroupAssignee.objects.assign(group, user) with no source
contracts.before_after: Before: assign() queued an outbound sync to every linked external issue with no source. After: the source is passed through sync_group_assignee_outbound to the task, and the task skips outbound for the integration that sent the webhook.
contracts.visible_effect: The Sentry assignee changes as before. The integration that sent the assignment is no longer sent an echo of it, and the other linked integrations still receive the change.
contracts.failure_mode: If the dict cannot be parsed, from_dict returns None and the echo goes through silently (see the from_dict finding). apply_async is still called synchronously from assign(), so a queueing error propagates into the webhook request as before. This PR does not change that.

contracts.action: Inbound webhook unassigns a Sentry issue (sync_group_assignee_inbound with assign=False passes AssignmentSource to deassign)
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96 before the PR: GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(group) with no source
contracts.before_after: Before: deassign() queued an unassign to every linked external issue. After: the same, plus the source, so the sending integration is skipped.
contracts.visible_effect: The Sentry assignee is cleared as before. The sending integration is not told to unassign again.
contracts.failure_mode: The same as the assign path: a parse failure silently re-enables the echo.

contracts.action: Task calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound with the new assignment_source kwarg
contracts.equivalent_path: the same task before the PR: installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign)
contracts.before_after: The call now adds assignment_source=... . Every implementation takes **kwargs, so the extra argument is ignored.
contracts.visible_effect: None. The external assignee is set exactly as before.
contracts.failure_mode: An integration whose sync_assignee_outbound lacks **kwargs would raise TypeError, and the task would retry. All four current implementations accept **kwargs.

contracts.equivalent_path: the same task before the PR: should_sync('outbound_assignee'); the other caller is where_should_sync (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:48), which still calls should_sync(key) with no source
contracts.before_after: Before: the check returned the config value. After: when the source's integration_id equals the org integration's integration_id, it returns False first.
contracts.visible_effect: An assignment that came from integration X is not pushed back to X. Other integrations still receive it.
contracts.failure_mode: A source that fails to parse becomes None and the check is skipped (see the from_dict finding).

contracts.action: Task rebuilds AssignmentSource from the queued dict (AssignmentSource.from_dict)
contracts.equivalent_path: no direct equivalent: this is new code
contracts.before_after: A dict of the dataclass fields becomes an instance. A non-empty dict that does not match returns None.
contracts.failure_mode: Any TypeError yields None with no log. The task then runs the outbound sync with no source, so the echo guard is skipped silently.

contracts.action: sync_group_assignee_outbound queues sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source_dict via apply_async(kwargs=...)
contracts.equivalent_path: the sibling task queue in tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:19 is a plain apply_async; before the PR this call passed three kwargs
contracts.before_after: Before: three kwargs. After: a fourth kwarg, which is a dict or None. The dict contains a datetime (queued).
contracts.failure_mode: Serialization is pickle (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741), so the datetime survives the trip. A task message queued before deploy has three kwargs, and the new default of None keeps it working. The PR body's reason for switching to dicts ('JSON instead of classes') does not match the pickle config. The dict form works either way.

contracts.action: Sentry user unassigns or reassigns through the API (deassign without a source)
contracts.equivalent_path: the same deassign path before the PR
contracts.before_after: assignment_source defaults to None, so the new branch behaves exactly as before. The source check in should_sync is skipped for None.
contracts.visible_effect: No change for user-initiated assignments; they still propagate to every linked integration.

summary: The change adds an AssignmentSource that travels with inbound assign/unassign events. It lets the outbound task skip pushing an assignment back to the integration that sent it. The loop guard works on the paths I traced, and every existing sync_assignee_outbound implementation accepts **kwargs. Celery uses pickle (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741), so the dict payload is fine, though the PR body's "JSON instead of classes" reason does not match the config. There are no blockers. The main defect is that `queued` is evaluated once at import time (assignment_source.py:18). The other findings are a silent fallback in from_dict, an unused abstract parameter, a test that skips the inbound path, and an open question about whether skipping by integration rather than by external issue is intended. I did not run the tests; the review was read-only.
